statement.excerpt: As I hope I’ve made clear, I believe the vast majority of AI data centers are the AI bubble’s subprime loans, and will collapse when they face the cold, harsh reality of “someone actually paying money for AI compute,”

from_speaker: the vast majority of AI data centers

our_interpretation: The plain reading is a forecast of widespread financial failure caused by insufficient paying demand for AI compute. The subprime comparison describes the proposed mechanism, not a separate numerical claim.

Collapse means default, insolvency, permanent closure, or abandonment because compute receipts cannot support the project's obligations. Share-price declines, construction delays, write-downs, and ordinary acquisitions alone do not qualify.
Vast majority means an overwhelming share of projects, substantially more than half. No precise percentage is supplied, so borderline findings would remain unresolved.

The working population is AI data centers operating or being developed when the post appeared, across owners and countries. Counting projects rather than companies or megawatts is an evaluator interpretation.

The payment condition means projects have reached the stage when actual compute receipts must sustain their financial obligations. Evidence that individual operators have customers does not establish that this test has occurred across the claimed population.
The nearby reference to four years concerns operating-expense expectations; it does not clearly give this collapse forecast a deadline.
criteria.support_condition: Records establish that an overwhelming share of the relevant AI data-center projects defaulted, became insolvent, permanently closed, or were abandoned after reaching the payment test, with inadequate paying compute demand materially causing those failures.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Completed project and financing records establish that enough of the relevant population passed the payment test and completed their financial obligations without collapse to rule out failure of a vast majority. Continued operation at an interim date is insufficient.
